reference_id: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures
reference_title: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures, 1993 Edition

sections.title: Summary of Part I
sections.summary: Closes Part I with a brief recap: pavement design retains the AASHO-Road-Test-derived performance equations as the basic design model, now expanded with reliability, resilient-modulus-based material characterization, drainage, environmental (swelling/frost heave), and life-cycle-cost considerations, all detailed and applied in Parts II-IV.
sections.body: Part I's closing chapter (condensed here; printed guide pdf_page ~86-88, printed I-65) summarizes that the Guide retains the AASHO Road Test performance-prediction equations (as modified through the 1972/1981 Interim Guides) as its core empirical design model, now substantially expanded relative to earlier editions via the 14 major considerations enumerated in the Preface (reliability, resilient-modulus-based soil support and layer coefficients, drainage, improved environmental treatment, tied shoulders/widened lanes, subbase erosion, life-cycle costs, rehabilitation, pavement management, extended load equivalency values, improved traffic data, low-volume-road design, and mechanistic-empirical state-of-knowledge).
key_points: Core design model remains the AASHO Road Test performance-prediction equations
1993 edition substantially expands the 1972/1981 Interim Guides via the 14 major new considerations (see Preface)
Parts II-IV apply/detail these considerations for new-pavement design, rehabilitation, and mechanistic-empirical state-of-knowledge respectively
sections.applicability: Transition/summary between Part I's background material and the Part II design procedures.
